## Findings ledger
- [D4.DOC21.F1] The chapter builds on Weber indirectly by reporting that Emigh et al. combined Weber with Gramsci to analyse intellectual interventions across micro-, meso-, and macro-levels — dim: citation_stance — anchor: "by combining Weber with Gramsci, investigated the micro-level social interactional backdrop to common sense as well as the macro-level political effects of intellectuals’ alignment" — doc: em:EZWD7IBR — ref: p. 29 — stance: builds_on — object: Emigh et al.’s combination of Weber with Gramsci to investigate the micro-level interactional and macro-level political effects of intellectuals — anchor-b: "Their work then showed how intellectual interventions have implications at various levels of the social structure (micro, meso, and macro)." — doc-b: em:EZWD7IBR — confidence: high — trimmed-anchor: yes

sections_inspected: Chapter 2, pp. 25–50, especially pp. 29–30 and the reference list
scope_outcomes.criterion: A passage must state how the citing text adopts, builds on, qualifies, disputes, or merely mentions a proposition attributed to Weber.
scope_outcomes.basis: The chapter reports that Emigh et al. combined Weber with Gramsci to investigate intellectuals’ micro-level interactions and macro-level political effects, presenting the cited work as a basis for its literature review.
limitations: The passage attributes the combination to Emigh et al. rather than presenting a detailed Weberian proposition developed directly by the four chapter authors.
This assessment covers the supplied chapter text, not the authors’ complete work or Weber’s entire reception.

evidence_state.coverage_basis: reader/reviewer report; source bytes do not establish inspection or completeness
blocking_issues: One or more declared finding references lack retained verified evidence
